picks.title: Sitting Like a Buddha
picks.summary: Where are you located in your body? Most of us, without ever having chosen it, sense ourselves somewhere behind the eyes. Zazen instructions typically bundle two separable practices: disidentifying from thinking, and relocating the self in the belly. Contemporary mindfulness often teaches the first and omits the second. Zen's own instruction is to sit as a buddha rather than in order to become one, trusting a monastic container to do that work silently; outside such a container, this talk suggests, it has to be made explicit. picks.reason: Instructions on sitting as Buddha focus on embodied presence and non-self in Zen practice.

picks.showTitle: Zen Stories & Buddhist Teachings for Sleep by Midnight Monk
picks.title: Buddhist Stories to Help You Let Go and Fall Asleep - Zen Buddhism for Rest
picks.summary: Tonight, we slow down and practice the quiet art of letting go. Through Zen stories for sleep and gentle Buddhist teachings, we explore attachment, acceptance, self-compassion, and the peace that appears when we stop holding on so tightly. Nothing here needs to be studied or remembered. picks.reason: Zen Buddhist stories and teachings on impermanence and letting go for restful sleep.
